objections: Every retrieved item is off-domain: three identical World Bank indicator searches return only agricultural metrics (fertilizer consumption, arable land), and two OpenAlex searches return an NLP paper on sell-side reports (arXiv 2411.13813) and a 2015 Dieter Ernst paper on China/forging policy. Not one item contains an Intel financial figure, a consensus estimate, guidance, or segment data. Any directional lean on 'above consensus' is therefore refuted by total evidentiary absence — there is literally zero Intel-specific datum in the record, and the record itself flags all sub-questions [GAP: unprovable] or UNVERIFIED 0.00.

The same observed pattern — a research dossier assembled on this question — is fully explained by a retrieval-routing failure: full-question strings were piped as keyword searches into the World Bank indicator API (source=2) and OpenAlex fulltext.search, sources that structurally cannot hold analyst consensus or earnings data. Under that mechanism, whatever stance or confidence the pipeline attaches to the conclusion is noise from the query plumbing, not signal about Intel.

The two academic hits are keyword-coincidence matches ('analyst', 'earnings', 'consensus' in an NLP abstract; 'forging' matched to 'foundry' in the Ernst paper). A pipeline that ingests such near-miss documents as 'evidence' creates survivorship of lexically similar but substantively empty sources; repeated across many questions, this process manufactures apparent corroboration for arbitrary conclusions regardless of the true base rate of beats vs misses (~50% by chance for EPS).

The single most likely artifact: because consensus expectations are absent, any 'beat' determination reduces to a coin flip around the ~50% historical beat rate, so an affirmative answer would look correct roughly half the time purely by chance — and the SPECULATIVE 0.54 confidence scores sit almost exactly at that coin-flip level, indicating the pipeline's stated probability reflects default prior positioning in the absence of evidence rather than any information about Intel's next quarter.
